name: Privacy Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal privacy policy governing the collection, processing, use, and protection of personal data for all staff and customers. The policy is owned by the Data Protection Officer and maintained by the Compliance Department, effective from 2026-01-15 with a review date of 2027-01-15.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: The EU General Data Protection Regulation (EU 2016/679) is a primary regulatory basis for FirstUK Bank's privacy policy, establishing requirements for personal data processing and protection across the European Union.

name: Data Protection Act 2018
description: UK legislation that implements and supplements GDPR requirements within the United Kingdom, forming part of the regulatory basis for FirstUK Bank's privacy policy.
context: Regulatory Reference | GDPR (EU 2016/679), Data Protection Act 2018

name: Data Protection Officer
description: The Data Protection Officer is designated as the owner of FirstUK Bank's Privacy Policy, responsible for its governance, maintenance, and compliance oversight.

name: All Staff
description: All FirstUK Bank employees are identified as an audience for the Privacy Policy, indicating they have obligations and responsibilities under the policy.

name: Customer
description: FirstUK Bank customers are identified as a primary audience for the Privacy Policy, indicating they are data subjects whose personal data is processed under the policy's governance.

name: Data Protection Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy establishing procedures for data collection, processing, storage, and customer rights management in compliance with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act 2018. The policy commits the bank to protecting customer personal data across all operations.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to protecting customer personal data in compliance with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act 2018
This policy establishes procedures for data collection, processing, storage, and customer rights management

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU regulation establishing data protection requirements that FirstUK Bank must comply with regarding customer personal data handling, processing, and rights.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to protecting customer personal data in compliance with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act 2018

name: UK Data Protection Act 2018
description: UK legislation establishing data protection requirements that FirstUK Bank must comply with for customer personal data handling and processing.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to protecting customer personal data in compliance with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act 2018

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorized access, loss, or compromise of customer personal data that the Data Protection Policy is designed to mitigate through controlled collection, processing, and storage procedures.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to protecting customer personal data

name: Personal Data Protection Policy
description: A formal policy establishing procedures for personal data protection that comply with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act. The policy governs customer privacy rights, data security, subject access requests, and implementation of data subject rights including access, erasure, and portability.
context: To establish procedures for personal data protection that: Comply with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act
Secure personal data against unauthorized access
Implement data subject rights (access, erasure, portability)

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU regulation establishing requirements for personal data protection and privacy rights. This policy must comply with GDPR requirements.
context: Comply with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act

name: UK Data Protection Act
description: UK legislation governing personal data protection and privacy. This policy must comply with UK Data Protection Act requirements.
context: Comply with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act

name: Unauthorized Data Access
description: The risk of personal data being accessed without authorization. The policy addresses this risk through data security measures and access controls.
context: Secure personal data against unauthorized access

name: Privacy Rights Violation
description: The risk of failing to respect and uphold customer privacy rights. The policy mitigates this through procedures that respect customer privacy rights.

name: Compliance with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act
description: Mandatory requirement to ensure all personal data protection procedures comply with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act requirements.
context: Comply with GDPR and UK Data Protection Act

name: Customer Privacy Rights Protection
description: Obligation to respect and protect customer privacy rights throughout all data handling processes.

name: Personal Data Security Against Unauthorized Access
description: Mandatory requirement to implement security measures that protect personal data against unauthorized access.
context: Secure personal data against unauthorized access

name: Customer Subject Access Request Management
description: Obligation to establish and maintain procedures for managing customer subject access requests in compliance with data protection regulations.

name: Implementation of Data Subject Rights
description: Mandatory requirement to implement and facilitate data subject rights including access, erasure, and portability of personal data.
context: Implement data subject rights (access, erasure, portability)

name: Data Security Controls
description: Operational safeguards implemented to secure personal data against unauthorized access. These controls are required to protect customer information throughout its lifecycle.
context: Secure personal data against unauthorized access

name: Subject Access Request Processing
description: Operational procedure for receiving, processing, and responding to customer subject access requests in compliance with regulatory requirements.

name: Customer
description: Natural persons who hold banking relationships and whose personal data is subject to protection under this policy. Customers have privacy rights and can exercise data subject rights.
context: Implement data subject rights (access, erasure, portability)

name: Data Protection Policy
description: A comprehensive policy governing the handling, processing, and protection of customer personal data and staff information across all systems, storage, and data processing activities within the organization.
context: Applies to: All customer personal data

name: Customer Personal Data Protection Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to protect and appropriately handle all customer personal data across the organization's operations.

name: Staff and Contractor Data Handling Obligation
description: Obligation to ensure all staff and contractors comply with data protection requirements in their handling of personal data.

name: Data Processing Activities Governance
description: Requirement to govern and control all data processing activities conducted by the organization to ensure compliance with data protection standards.

name: Systems and Storage Security Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to implement appropriate security controls across all systems and storage facilities handling personal data.

name: All Staff
description: All staff members are responsible for complying with data protection requirements in their handling of customer personal data and organizational information.

name: Contractors
description: All contractors engaged by the organization are subject to the same data protection obligations as staff members.

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorized access to, loss of, or compromise of customer personal data and staff information across systems and storage.

name: Data Access Control
description: Control mechanism to restrict and manage access to personal data across all systems and storage facilities.

name: Data Processing Activity Monitoring
description: Monitoring and logging mechanism to track all data processing activities to ensure compliance and detect unauthorized processing.

name: Data Processing and Customer Control Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's overarching policy governing the processing of customer personal data. The policy establishes that data processing occurs only where necessary for the delivery of banking services, with mandatory safeguards in place and explicit customer control mechanisms. This policy forms the foundation for the bank's data protection compliance framework.
context: FirstUK Bank processes customer personal data only where necessary for banking services
with proper safeguards and customer control

name: Necessity Limitation for Data Processing
description: Mandatory requirement that customer personal data processing by FirstUK Bank must be limited to only those instances where processing is necessary for the delivery of banking services. This provision establishes the principle of data minimisation and purpose limitation.
context: processes customer personal data only where necessary for banking services

name: Data Safeguards Implementation
description: Mandatory requirement that FirstUK Bank must implement and maintain proper safeguards when processing customer personal data. This provision establishes the bank's obligation to protect data through appropriate technical and organisational measures.
context: with proper safeguards and customer control

name: Customer Control Over Personal Data
description: Mandatory requirement that customers must retain meaningful control over their personal data processed by FirstUK Bank. This provision establishes customer rights to direct, consent to, or otherwise govern the use of their data.
context: with proper safeguards and customer control

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorised access to, loss of, or compromise of customer personal data. FirstUK Bank's data processing policy is designed to mitigate this risk through the implementation of proper safeguards.
context: with proper safeguards and customer control

name: Unauthorised Data Processing
description: The risk that customer personal data may be processed for purposes beyond what is necessary for banking services or without appropriate customer consent and control. The policy addresses this through necessity limitation and customer control mechanisms.
context: processes customer personal data only where necessary for banking services
with proper safeguards and customer control

name: Customer
description: Natural persons who hold banking relationships with FirstUK Bank and whose personal data is subject to processing under this policy. Customers retain control over their personal data and must be informed of processing activities.
context: FirstUK Bank processes customer personal data
with proper safeguards and customer control

name: Data Privacy and Protection Policy
description: A comprehensive policy governing the lawful processing, security, and retention of customer data within the bank. The policy establishes core requirements for transparency, data security, customer rights, and consent management in accordance with banking and regulatory standards.
context: Lawful Basis: Data processed only for banking/regulatory purposes
Transparency: Clear privacy notices provided to customers
Data Security: Encryption and access controls
Customer Rights: Subject access requests processed within 30 days

name: Lawful Basis for Data Processing
description: Establishes that all customer data must be processed exclusively for banking and regulatory purposes. This provision ensures the bank operates within legal boundaries when handling personal information.
context: Lawful Basis: Data processed only for banking/regulatory purposes

name: Transparency Through Privacy Notices
description: Requires the bank to provide clear and accessible privacy notices to all customers. This provision ensures customers are informed about how their data is collected, used, and protected.
context: Transparency: Clear privacy notices provided to customers

name: Data Security Through Encryption and Access Controls
description: Mandates implementation of encryption and access control mechanisms to protect customer data from unauthorized access and breach. This is a core technical safeguard requirement.
context: Data Security: Encryption and access controls

name: Subject Access Request Processing Timeframe
description: Establishes a mandatory 30-day processing window for customer subject access requests. This provision ensures timely fulfillment of customer rights to access their personal data.
context: Customer Rights: Subject access requests processed within 30 days

name: Data Retention Minimization
description: Requires the bank to retain customer data only for as long as necessary to fulfill banking and regulatory purposes. This provision implements the data minimization principle.
context: Retention: Data retained only as long as necessary

name: Explicit Consent for Marketing Communications
description: Mandates that the bank obtain explicit, informed consent from customers before sending marketing communications. This provision protects customer autonomy and complies with consent-based marketing standards.
context: Consent Management: Explicit consent for marketing communications

name: Data Encryption
description: A technical control requiring encryption of customer data to protect confidentiality and integrity. This safeguard prevents unauthorized access to sensitive banking information.
context: Data Security: Encryption and access controls

name: Access Control System
description: An operational control mechanism that restricts access to customer data based on role and necessity. This safeguard ensures only authorized personnel can view or modify sensitive information.
context: Data Security: Encryption and access controls

name: Data Protection Officer
description: An abstract role responsible for overseeing data protection compliance, privacy notice delivery, and customer rights fulfillment. The DPO ensures the bank meets all privacy and data security obligations.
context: Transparency: Clear privacy notices provided to customers
Customer Rights: Subject access requests processed within 30 days

name: All Staff
description: All bank employees are collectively responsible for adhering to data security, encryption, and access control requirements. Staff must respect customer privacy and handle data lawfully.
context: Data Security: Encryption and access controls
Lawful Basis: Data processed only for banking/regulatory purposes

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorized access to or compromise of customer personal data. This risk is mitigated through encryption, access controls, and data retention minimization.
context: Data Security: Encryption and access controls
Retention: Data retained only as long as necessary

name: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The risk that customer data is processed for purposes outside banking and regulatory functions. This risk is controlled through the lawful basis requirement and transparency measures.
context: Lawful Basis: Data processed only for banking/regulatory purposes
Transparency: Clear privacy notices provided to customers

name: Unauthorized Marketing Communication
description: The risk of sending marketing communications to customers without their explicit consent. This risk is mitigated through mandatory consent management procedures.
context: Consent Management: Explicit consent for marketing communications

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds a banking relationship with the bank and is subject to data privacy protections. Customers have rights to transparency, data security, and access to their personal information.
context: Transparency: Clear privacy notices provided to customers
Customer Rights: Subject access requests processed within 30 days

name: Data Processing and Retention Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's policy governing lawful bases for personal data processing across account management, KYC/AML compliance, fraud detection, marketing, regulatory reporting, and complaint handling. The policy establishes retention periods aligned with contractual necessity, legal obligation, and legitimate interest grounds.
context: Lawful Bases Used by FirstUK Bank
Account opening & management | Contractual necessity | Account tenure + 6 years
KYC/AML compliance | Legal obligation | 5-6 years post-closure

name: Account Opening and Management Data Retention
description: Requires retention of account opening and management data for the duration of account tenure plus 6 years thereafter, justified on the basis of contractual necessity.
context: Account opening & management | Contractual necessity | Account tenure + 6 years

name: KYC/AML Compliance Data Retention
description: Mandates retention of KYC/AML compliance data for 5-6 years following account closure, grounded in legal obligation to maintain audit trails and compliance evidence.
context: KYC/AML compliance | Legal obligation | 5-6 years post-closure

name: Fraud Detection Data Retention
description: Specifies retention of fraud detection data for 3 years, justified on the basis of legitimate interest in protecting the bank and its customers from financial crime.

name: Marketing Consent Data Retention
description: Requires retention of marketing data only where explicit customer consent has been obtained, with retention continuing until the customer withdraws consent.
context: Marketing (if consented) | Explicit consent | Until withdrawal

name: Regulatory Reporting Data Retention
description: Mandates retention of regulatory reporting data in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, typically 5-7 years, to satisfy legal obligation obligations.
context: Regulatory reporting | Legal obligation | Per regulation (5-7 years)

name: Complaint Handling Data Retention
description: Requires retention of complaint handling data for 8 weeks as mandated by FCA requirements, grounded in both contractual and legal obligations.
context: Complaint handling | Contractual & legal | 8 weeks (FCA requirement)

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The data controller responsible for establishing and implementing lawful bases for personal data processing across all banking operations and ensuring compliance with retention schedules.
context: Lawful Bases Used by FirstUK Bank

name: Fraud
description: Financial crime risk addressed through fraud detection data processing and retention for 3 years on the basis of legitimate interest.

name: Money Laundering
description: Financial crime risk mitigated through KYC/AML compliance data processing and retention for 5-6 years post-closure as a legal obligation.
context: KYC/AML compliance | Legal obligation | 5-6 years post-closure

name: KYC Verification
description: Customer identity and compliance verification process conducted at account opening and maintained throughout the account lifecycle, with supporting data retained for 5-6 years post-closure.
context: KYC/AML compliance | Legal obligation | 5-6 years post-closure

name: AML Screening
description: Ongoing anti-money laundering screening and monitoring process required as a legal obligation, with compliance data retained for 5-6 years following account closure.
context: KYC/AML compliance | Legal obligation | 5-6 years post-closure

name: Data Collection Policy
description: Policy governing the collection of customer identity, financial, behavioral, and device data. Establishes the scope and categories of personal information collected across account opening, transaction monitoring, fraud detection, and customer service interactions.
context: Identity Data: Full name, date of birth, nationality
Financial Data: Account balances, transaction history
Behavioral Data: Transaction patterns (for fraud detection)

name: Fraud Detection
description: Risk category addressed through collection and analysis of transaction patterns and behavioral data. The policy identifies fraud detection as a key purpose for monitoring customer transaction patterns and device information.
context: Behavioral Data: Transaction patterns (for fraud detection)

name: Transaction Pattern Monitoring
description: Operational control mechanism that collects and analyzes customer transaction patterns as part of behavioral data collection. Used to detect fraudulent activity and unusual account behavior.
context: Behavioral Data: Transaction patterns (for fraud detection)

name: Identification Document
description: Official identity documents collected as part of identity data during customer onboarding. The policy specifies that identification documents are collected but does not detail specific document types or validity requirements in this passage.
context: Identity Data: Full name, date of birth, nationality, Contact details (email, phone, address), Identification documents

name: Customer
description: Natural person subject to data collection under this policy. Customers are the data subjects whose identity, financial, behavioral, and device information is collected across banking products and services.

name: Identity Verification
description: The process of collecting and verifying customer identity through verification documents such as passports. This is performed at account opening and through direct customer submission of supporting documentation.
context: Direct from customer (account forms, online signup)

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying customer address through utility bills and other proof of address documentation collected directly from customers or third parties.
context: Direct from customer (account forms, online signup)

name: Passport
description: An official identity document accepted as verification documentation for KYC purposes during account opening and customer verification processes.

name: Utility Bill
description: An official document accepted as verification documentation for address verification and KYC purposes, collected directly from customers.

name: Cookies and Analytics Tracking
description: The collection of customer data through cookies and analytics mechanisms on the bank's website and mobile application to track user behaviour and interactions.

name: Automated Transaction Records
description: The automated collection and retention of customer transaction data and system records generated through banking systems and customer transactions.

name: Credit Bureau
description: Third-party credit bureaus that provide customer information and credit data to the bank for mortgage and lending decisions.

name: Privacy Notice Policy
description: Policy governing the provision and content of privacy notices to customers at key touchpoints including account opening, online signup, and on request. Establishes mandatory disclosure of data controller identity, processing purposes, lawful basis, retention periods, customer rights, and data query contact information.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Account opening (mandatory)
Privacy Notice Contains: Data controller identity (FirstUK Bank)

name: Mandatory Privacy Notice at Account Opening
description: Requirement that a privacy notice must be provided to customers at the point of account opening. This is explicitly marked as a mandatory disclosure obligation.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Account opening (mandatory)

name: Privacy Notice Provision at Online and Mobile App Signup
description: Requirement that privacy notices must be made available to customers during online and mobile application signup processes.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Online/mobile app signup

name: Privacy Notice Publication on Website
description: Requirement that a privacy notice be published as a public notice on the bank's website for general access.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Website (public notice)

name: Privacy Notice Provision on Customer Request
description: Requirement that privacy notices must be provided to customers upon request at any time.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: On request

name: Data Controller Identity Disclosure
description: Requirement that privacy notices must disclose the identity of the data controller, identified as FirstUK Bank.
context: Privacy Notice Contains: Data controller identity (FirstUK Bank)

name: Processing Purposes Disclosure
description: Requirement that privacy notices must clearly disclose the purposes for which customer personal data is processed.

name: Lawful Basis Disclosure
description: Requirement that privacy notices must disclose the lawful basis upon which the bank processes customer personal data.

name: Data Retention Period Disclosure
description: Requirement that privacy notices must disclose the period for which customer personal data is retained.
context: Privacy Notice Contains: Data retention period

name: Customer Rights Disclosure
description: Requirement that privacy notices must disclose the rights available to customers regarding their personal data.

name: Data Query Contact Information Disclosure
description: Requirement that privacy notices must provide contact information for customers to direct data-related queries and requests.
context: Privacy Notice Contains: Contact for data queries

name: Data Privacy Risk
description: Risk of non-compliance with data protection obligations and failure to provide transparent notice to customers regarding personal data processing, retention, and customer rights.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Account opening (mandatory)
Privacy Notice Contains: Data controller identity (FirstUK Bank)

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The data controller and policy owner responsible for implementing privacy notice requirements and disclosing personal data processing activities to customers.

name: New Account
description: Customer account at the point of opening, which triggers the mandatory provision of a privacy notice.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Account opening (mandatory)

name: Customer
description: Natural person who holds or applies for a banking account and is entitled to receive privacy notices disclosing how their personal data is processed.
context: Privacy Notice Provided At: Account opening (mandatory)

name: Data Subject Rights Policy
description: Policy governing the exercise of data subject rights under GDPR, specifically the right of access to personal data held by the bank. Establishes the process for customers to request copies of their personal data, including verification requirements, response timelines, and format of delivery.
context: Request copy of personal data held

name: Right of Access Request Submission
description: Customers must submit written requests for access to personal data to the designated email address privacy@firstuk.bank. This is the mandatory entry point for exercising the right of access.

name: Identity Verification for Access Requests
description: The bank must verify the identity of the customer submitting a right of access request for security purposes before processing the request. This safeguard protects against unauthorized disclosure of personal data.

name: Right of Access Response Timeframe
description: The bank must respond to right of access requests within 30 calendar days, or within 60 days if the request is complex. This implements the GDPR statutory response deadline.
context: Response within 30 days (or 60 days if complex)

name: Data Provision in Electronic Format
description: Personal data provided in response to a right of access request must be delivered in electronic format. This ensures accessibility and compliance with GDPR requirements for data portability.

name: Right of Access Fee Exemption
description: The bank must not charge a fee for providing access to personal data, except in cases where requests are excessive. This reflects the GDPR principle that data subject rights should be exercised without cost.

name: Regulatory Reference
description: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the primary regulatory basis for this policy. It establishes the legal framework for data subject rights, including the right of access to personal data.

name: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: The risk that personal data could be disclosed to unauthorized individuals if identity verification is not properly conducted before providing access to customer data.

name: Identity Verification Control
description: A security control requiring verification of customer identity before processing and responding to right of access requests. This prevents unauthorized disclosure of personal data.

name: Data Protection Officer
description: The role responsible for overseeing compliance with GDPR data subject rights, including processing right of access requests and ensuring timely, accurate responses to customers.

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds a banking relationship with the bank and has the right to request access to their personal data held by the bank under GDPR.
context: Customer Right: Request copy of personal data held

name: Right of Access Verification
description: The identity verification process required before the bank provides personal data in response to a right of access request. This ensures that only the legitimate data subject receives their personal information.

name: Right to Erasure Policy
description: Policy governing the conditions under which customer personal data may be erased or deleted, including the legal and operational exceptions that override erasure requests. The policy balances data subject rights against regulatory retention obligations and legitimate business interests.
context: Data no longer necessary for purpose

name: Data Necessity Assessment for Erasure
description: Requirement to evaluate whether personal data remains necessary for its original purpose before processing an erasure request. Data must be assessed as no longer necessary before erasure can be considered.
context: Data no longer necessary for purpose

name: Legal Obligation Retention Override
description: Prohibition on erasure when a legal or regulatory obligation requires data retention. Specifically applies to AML and KYC records which must be retained regardless of erasure requests.

name: Legitimate Interest Retention Override
description: Prohibition on erasure when the bank has a documented legitimate interest in retaining the data. Overrides erasure requests when legitimate business interests are identified.

name: Consent Withdrawal Erasure Trigger
description: Requirement to process erasure requests when consent is the legal basis for processing and the customer withdraws that consent. Applies only when consent was the original lawful basis.

name: Dispute and Complaint Data Retention
description: Prohibition on erasure of data when ongoing disputes or complaints exist. Data must be retained to support resolution and investigation of customer disputes.

name: Fraud Investigation Data Retention
description: Prohibition on erasure of data when fraud investigation is active or pending. Data must be retained to support fraud detection, investigation, and prevention activities.

name: Financial Claim Data Retention
description: Prohibition on erasure of data when a financial claim is pending against the customer or the bank. Data must be retained to support claim resolution and potential litigation.

name: Active Account or Product Data Retention
description: Prohibition on erasure of data relating to active customer accounts or products. Data must be retained while the customer maintains an active banking relationship.

name: Anti-Money Laundering Records
description: Regulatory requirement to retain customer identification and transaction records for anti-money laundering purposes. Referenced as a mandatory exception to data erasure requests.

name: Know Your Customer Records
description: Regulatory requirement to retain customer identity verification and due diligence documentation. Referenced as a mandatory exception to data erasure requests.

name: Fraud Risk
description: Risk of fraudulent activity by customers or third parties. The policy identifies fraud investigation as a legitimate reason to retain customer data despite erasure requests.

name: Compliance and Regulatory Risk
description: Risk of regulatory non-compliance and sanctions resulting from improper data retention or erasure. The policy balances data subject rights against mandatory regulatory retention obligations.

name: Dispute and Complaint Risk
description: Risk of unresolved customer disputes and complaints. The policy identifies ongoing disputes as a reason to retain data for investigation and resolution.

name: Financial Claim Risk
description: Risk of financial claims and potential litigation. The policy identifies pending financial claims as a reason to retain customer data.

name: Data Rectification Policy
description: Policy governing customer rights to correct inaccurate personal data held by FirstUK Bank. Establishes the process for submitting correction requests, verification procedures, system update timelines, and third-party notification obligations.

name: Correction Request Submission
description: Customers must submit a correction request to initiate the data rectification process. This is the first step in exercising the right to rectification.

name: Bank Verification of Requested Change
description: FirstUK Bank must verify the accuracy and validity of the requested data correction before proceeding with system updates.

name: System Update Within 30 Days
description: Upon verification of a correction request, FirstUK Bank must update its systems to reflect the corrected data within 30 days.

name: Third Party Notification of Data Correction
description: FirstUK Bank must notify any third parties to whom the inaccurate data was previously shared, informing them of the correction made.
context: Notify third parties if data shared

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The bank responsible for implementing the data rectification policy, including verification of correction requests, system updates, and third-party notification.
context: Notify third parties if data shared

name: Customer
description: The individual who holds a banking relationship with FirstUK Bank and possesses the right to request correction of inaccurate personal data.

name: Right to Restrict Processing Policy
description: Policy governing the customer right to restrict processing of personal data without requiring deletion. Applies when customers dispute data accuracy or wish to limit processing scope while disputes are resolved. Data marked as restricted in system with processing limited to legal obligations only.
context: Limit how data used (but not require deletion)
Limited processing only for legal obligations

name: Customer Right to Dispute Data Accuracy
description: Provision enabling customers to dispute the accuracy of personal data held by the bank. Upon dispute, data processing is restricted pending resolution of the accuracy challenge.
context: Data processing while accuracy under dispute

name: Data Restriction Marking in System
description: Requirement to mark disputed or restricted data as 'restricted' within the bank's data management systems to prevent unauthorized or unnecessary processing.

name: Limited Processing During Restriction Period
description: Obligation to limit data processing to legal obligations only when data has been marked as restricted due to accuracy disputes or customer restriction requests.
context: Limited processing only for legal obligations

name: Data Accuracy Risk
description: Risk that personal data held by the bank may be inaccurate or outdated, potentially leading to incorrect decisions or customer harm. This policy addresses mitigation through customer dispute rights and processing restrictions.
context: Data processing while accuracy under dispute

name: Data Restriction Flagging System
description: Technical control measure that flags or marks customer data as 'restricted' within the bank's systems to prevent processing beyond legal obligations while accuracy disputes are pending.
context: Limited processing only for legal obligations

name: Customer
description: Individual customer with the right to restrict processing of their personal data, including the ability to dispute data accuracy and request limitation of processing scope.
context: Customer Right: Limit how data used

name: Data Portability Policy
description: Policy governing customer rights to obtain personal data in portable format for transfer to another provider. Establishes the process, timeframe, and data scope for fulfilling data portability requests.
context: Obtain data in portable format for transfer to another provider
Data provided in common electronic format (CSV, JSON)
Applies to data provided by customer or generated through use

name: Data Portability Request Submission
description: Customers must submit a written request specifying the data they wish to obtain in portable format. This is the mandatory first step in the data portability process.

name: Data Provision in Common Electronic Format
description: The bank must provide requested data in common electronic formats such as CSV or JSON to enable portability and transfer to another provider.
context: Data provided in common electronic format (CSV, JSON)

name: Data Portability Response Timeframe
description: The bank must respond to data portability requests within 30 days of receipt. This establishes the maximum permissible response period for fulfilling customer data portability rights.

name: Data Portability Scope Definition
description: Data portability applies to all data provided by the customer or generated through their use of the bank's services. This defines the scope of data subject to portability requests.
context: Applies to data provided by customer or generated through use

name: Data Portability Right
description: The regulatory and operational risk associated with ensuring customers can exercise their right to obtain and transfer their personal data in portable format. Non-compliance exposes the bank to regulatory sanctions and customer disputes.
context: Obtain data in portable format for transfer to another provider

name: Customer
description: The natural person who holds a banking relationship and possesses the right to request their personal data in portable format for transfer to another provider.
context: Customer Right: Obtain data in portable format for transfer to another provider
Applies to data provided by customer or generated through use

name: Right to Object Policy
description: Policy governing customer rights to object to data processing, including direct marketing, profiling, automated decision-making, and legitimate interest processing. Establishes mandatory opt-out mechanisms across email, phone, and SMS channels with immediate system recording.
context: Legitimate interest processing: Can object if no compelling reason

name: Mandatory Direct Marketing Opt-Out
description: Customers must be provided with the ability to opt out of direct marketing communications. This is a mandatory provision that applies to all direct marketing activities.

name: Profiling and Automated Decision Objection Right
description: Customers have the right to object to profiling and automated decision-making processes conducted by the bank.

name: Legitimate Interest Processing Objection Right
description: Customers may object to processing based on legitimate interest grounds if the bank has no compelling reason to continue processing.
context: Legitimate interest processing: Can object if no compelling reason

name: Email Marketing Preference Management
description: Every marketing email must include a link enabling customers to manage their email marketing preferences and opt out.
context: Email preference: link in every marketing email

name: Phone Marketing Preference Request Process
description: Customers may request to opt out of phone marketing by contacting the support team.
context: Phone preference: request to support team

name: SMS Marketing Opt-Out Mechanism
description: Customers can opt out of SMS marketing by texting 'STOP' to the designated number provided in marketing messages.

name: Immediate Recording of Opt-Out Preferences
description: All customer opt-out preferences and objections must be recorded immediately in the bank's system to ensure compliance and prevent further unwanted communications.

name: Marketing Email Preference Link
description: Technical control requiring inclusion of an opt-out link in every marketing email to enable customers to manage preferences.
context: Email preference: link in every marketing email

name: SMS Stop Command Processing
description: Operational control enabling customers to send 'STOP' text messages to opt out of SMS marketing, with immediate system processing.

name: Preference Recording System
description: System control that records all customer opt-out preferences and objections immediately upon receipt to maintain audit trail and prevent non-compliance.

name: Direct Marketing
description: Risk of non-compliance with customer preferences regarding direct marketing communications across email, phone, and SMS channels.

name: Profiling and Automated Decision-Making
description: Risk of processing customer data through profiling or automated decision-making without respecting customer objection rights.

name: Legitimate Interest Processing Misuse
description: Risk of continuing to process customer data on legitimate interest grounds when customers have objected and the bank has no compelling reason to continue.
context: Legitimate interest processing: Can object if no compelling reason

name: Customer
description: Individual customers hold the right to object to processing, including direct marketing, profiling, automated decisions, and legitimate interest processing. Customers may exercise these rights through multiple channels.

name: Support Team
description: Support team is responsible for processing customer requests to opt out of phone marketing communications.
context: Phone preference: request to support team

name: Right to Not Be Subject to Automated Decisions
description: Policy establishing customer protections against high-impact automated decisions in banking operations. Requires human review for significant automated decisions and grants customers the right to be informed, request review, provide perspective, and appeal outcomes.
context: Right to Not Be Subject to Automated Decisions
High-impact automated decisions require human review

name: Human Review Requirement for High-Impact Automated Decisions
description: Mandatory requirement that high-impact automated decisions must be subject to human review before implementation or communication to the customer.
context: High-impact automated decisions require human review

name: Customer Notification of Automated Decision
description: Obligation to inform customers when an automated decision has been made that affects them, ensuring transparency in decision-making processes.

name: Customer Right to Request Human Review
description: Provision granting customers the explicit right to request human review of any automated decision made about them.

name: Customer Right to Provide Own Perspective
description: Requirement to allow customers to submit their own perspective or additional information for consideration in the review of an automated decision.

name: Customer Right to Appeal Automated Decision
description: Provision establishing the customer's right to formally appeal or challenge an automated decision through an appeals process.

name: Automated Decision Risk
description: Risk category encompassing the potential for high-impact automated decisions to unfairly or incorrectly affect customers without adequate human oversight or customer recourse.
context: High-impact automated decisions require human review

name: Human Review Gate for Automated Decisions
description: Control mechanism requiring human review and approval before high-impact automated decisions are finalized or communicated to customers.
context: High-impact automated decisions require human review

name: Automated Fraud Detection
description: Automated fraud detection system that may trigger account freezes or other protective actions, subject to human review and customer notification requirements.

name: Automated Lending Decision System
description: Automated system for evaluating lending applications (such as mortgage applications) that generates initial decisions subject to human review before final rejection or approval.

name: Automated Credit Scoring System
description: Automated system for calculating credit scores that impacts customer lending eligibility and terms, subject to human review and customer appeal rights.

name: Data Security Policy
description: Policy governing encryption and data protection requirements for customer and staff data in transit and at rest across all banking systems and channels.
context: In Transit: TLS 1.3 for all data transmission (web, mobile)
At Rest: AES-256 encryption for databases

name: TLS 1.3 Encryption for Data Transmission
description: Mandatory requirement to implement TLS 1.3 for all data transmission across web and mobile channels to protect data confidentiality during transit.
context: TLS 1.3 for all data transmission (web, mobile)

name: HTTPS Enforcement on Customer-Facing Systems
description: Mandatory requirement to enforce HTTPS protocol on all customer-facing systems to ensure encrypted communication channels.
context: HTTPS enforced on all customer-facing systems

name: VPN for Staff Remote Access
description: Mandatory requirement for staff to use VPN when accessing systems remotely to protect data transmission and maintain secure connectivity.

name: AES-256 Encryption for Databases
description: Mandatory requirement to encrypt all databases using AES-256 encryption standard to protect data at rest.

name: Encrypted Backups
description: Mandatory requirement to maintain encrypted backups stored on S3 and off-site locations to ensure data recovery capability with confidentiality protection.

name: Encrypted File Storage
description: Mandatory requirement to encrypt all file storage systems to protect data at rest across the organization.

name: Encrypted USB and Portable Device Storage
description: Mandatory requirement to encrypt all USB drives and portable devices used for data storage to prevent unauthorized access to data in transit.

name: TLS 1.3 Encryption
description: Cryptographic control implementing TLS 1.3 protocol for securing data transmission across web and mobile channels.
context: TLS 1.3 for all data transmission (web, mobile)

name: HTTPS Protocol Enforcement
description: Technical control enforcing HTTPS protocol on all customer-facing systems to ensure encrypted web communications.
context: HTTPS enforced on all customer-facing systems

name: VPN Access Control
description: Access control mechanism requiring staff to use VPN for remote access to protect data transmission and enforce secure connectivity.

name: AES-256 Database Encryption
description: Cryptographic control implementing AES-256 encryption standard for protecting database contents at rest.

name: Encrypted Backup Storage
description: Control mechanism for encrypting backup data stored on S3 and off-site locations to maintain confidentiality of recovery data.

name: File Storage Encryption
description: Cryptographic control for encrypting all file storage systems to protect data at rest.

name: Portable Device Encryption
description: Cryptographic control for encrypting USB drives and portable devices to prevent unauthorized access to data stored on removable media.

name: Data Breach
description: Risk of unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss of customer and staff data through unencrypted transmission or storage.

name: Unauthorized Access to Data in Transit
description: Risk of interception or eavesdropping on unencrypted data communications across web, mobile, and remote access channels.
context: In Transit: TLS 1.3 for all data transmission (web, mobile)

name: Unauthorized Access to Data at Rest
description: Risk of unauthorized access to unencrypted data stored in databases, backups, file systems, and portable devices.
context: At Rest: AES-256 encryption for databases

name: Access Control Policy
description: Policy governing role-based access to customer and operational data across the organisation. Defines access permissions by staff role, authentication requirements, and audit logging obligations to protect data confidentiality and integrity.
context: Role-Based Access: Customer-facing staff: Limited to customer data needed for service
Compliance staff: Full data access for regulatory purposes
Technology staff: Database access (with audit logging)
Executives: Aggregated data only (no personal details)

name: Customer-Facing Staff Data Access Limitation
description: Mandatory requirement restricting customer-facing staff access to only the customer data necessary to deliver service. Prevents unnecessary exposure of personal information.
context: Customer-facing staff: Limited to customer data needed for service

name: Compliance Staff Full Data Access for Regulatory Purposes
description: Mandatory requirement granting compliance staff full access to organisational data to fulfil regulatory obligations and conduct compliance monitoring.
context: Compliance staff: Full data access for regulatory purposes

name: Technology Staff Database Access with Audit Logging
description: Mandatory requirement permitting technology staff database access while requiring comprehensive audit logging of all database access events for accountability and security monitoring.
context: Technology staff: Database access (with audit logging)

name: Executive Access to Aggregated Data Only
description: Mandatory requirement restricting executive access to aggregated data summaries, explicitly prohibiting access to personal customer details to maintain data minimisation principles.
context: Executives: Aggregated data only (no personal details)

name: Multi-Factor Authentication for Admin and Compliance Access
description: Mandatory requirement implementing multi-factor authentication (username/password plus OTP) for all administrative and compliance staff accessing sensitive systems and data.

name: Audit Logging of All Access Events
description: Mandatory requirement to maintain comprehensive audit logs of all access to systems and data, enabling detection of unauthorised access and supporting compliance investigations.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication System
description: Technical control requiring username/password credentials combined with one-time password (OTP) authentication for administrative and compliance staff accessing sensitive systems.

name: Access Audit Logging
description: Operational control recording all access events to systems and data, including technology staff database access and all user authentication events, for security monitoring and compliance verification.

name: Customer-Facing Staff
description: Staff role with responsibility to access only customer data necessary for service delivery, subject to role-based access controls limiting data exposure.
context: Customer-facing staff: Limited to customer data needed for service

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff role with responsibility for regulatory compliance, granted full organisational data access to conduct compliance monitoring, investigations, and regulatory reporting.
context: Compliance staff: Full data access for regulatory purposes

name: Technology Staff
description: Staff role responsible for database and system administration, granted database access subject to comprehensive audit logging of all access events.
context: Technology staff: Database access (with audit logging)

name: Executives
description: Senior management role restricted to access of aggregated data summaries only, explicitly prohibited from accessing personal customer details.
context: Executives: Aggregated data only (no personal details)

name: Unauthorised Data Access
description: Risk of staff accessing customer or operational data beyond their role-based permissions, potentially exposing sensitive information or enabling fraud.
context: Role-Based Access: Customer-facing staff: Limited to customer data needed for service

name: Compliance Failure Due to Insufficient Data Access
description: Risk that compliance staff lack necessary data access to fulfil regulatory obligations, resulting in incomplete investigations or failed regulatory reporting.
context: Compliance staff: Full data access for regulatory purposes

name: Data Breach Response Policy
description: Policy governing the bank's response to data breaches, including notification obligations under GDPR, internal escalation procedures, risk assessment, and regulatory reporting requirements to the ICO.
context: If breach likely to cause high risk to individuals

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU regulation establishing data protection and privacy requirements, including mandatory breach notification timelines and individual notification obligations.

name: Data Breach
description: Unauthorized access to, loss of, or compromise of personal data held by the bank, characterized by potential high risk to individuals and triggering mandatory notification and regulatory reporting obligations.
context: If breach likely to cause high risk to individuals
Breach identified → Escalate to Data Protection Officer

name: Mandatory Individual Notification on High-Risk Breach
description: Requirement to notify affected individuals within 72 hours of identifying a data breach likely to cause high risk, including details of what happened, data affected, mitigation steps, and contact information.
context: If breach likely to cause high risk to individuals
Notification includes: What happened, what data, mitigation steps, contact for questions

name: Internal Breach Escalation to Data Protection Officer
description: Requirement to escalate any identified data breach to the Data Protection Officer immediately upon discovery, triggering internal investigation and risk assessment procedures.
context: Breach identified → Escalate to Data Protection Officer

name: Breach Investigation and Risk Assessment
description: Requirement to conduct investigation of identified breach within 24 hours and assess the risk level to determine notification and regulatory reporting obligations.

name: Regulatory Notification to ICO
description: Requirement to notify the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) when a data breach meets regulatory thresholds, following completion of internal risk assessment.

name: Data Protection Officer
description: Role responsible for receiving breach escalations, overseeing breach investigations, assessing risk levels, and determining notification and regulatory reporting decisions.

name: Breach Investigation Process
description: Operational control requiring investigation of data breaches within 24 hours to determine scope, affected data, and risk level to individuals.

name: Cookies and Web Tracking Policy
description: Policy governing the use of cookies and web tracking technologies on the bank's digital platforms. Distinguishes between essential cookies that do not require consent and optional cookies that require explicit customer consent.

name: Essential Cookies Deployment Without Consent
description: Provision permitting the deployment of session, security, and performance cookies without requiring prior customer consent, as these are necessary for core banking functionality and fraud prevention.

name: Optional Cookies Consent Requirement
description: Provision requiring explicit customer consent before deploying analytics and marketing cookies used for user behavior tracking, personalized advertising, and retargeting.

name: Fraud Prevention Risk
description: Risk category addressed through the deployment of security cookies to detect and prevent fraudulent activity on customer accounts and transactions.

name: Session Cookie Control
description: Essential control measure using session cookies to maintain secure login sessions and manage customer authentication on the bank's digital platforms.

name: Security Cookie Control
description: Essential control measure deploying security cookies to detect and prevent fraudulent transactions and unauthorized account access.

name: Performance Cookie Monitoring
description: Essential control measure using performance cookies to track system errors and monitor the technical performance of the bank's digital platforms.

name: Analytics Cookie Tracking
description: Optional control measure deploying analytics cookies to track and analyze customer behavior patterns on the bank's digital platforms, subject to explicit consent.

name: Marketing Cookie Deployment
description: Optional control measure using marketing cookies to enable personalized advertising and retargeting of customers across digital channels, subject to explicit consent.

name: Cookie Management Policy
description: Policy governing the bank's use of cookies on its website, including customer choice mechanisms, consent management, and third-party analytics practices. Establishes requirements for cookie banners, preference centers, and data retention for analytics services.

name: Cookie Banner Display Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to display a cookie banner on the bank's website to inform customers about cookie usage and obtain consent.

name: Non-Essential Cookie Acceptance Option
description: Requirement to provide customers with the option to accept or reject non-essential cookies, enabling granular consent control.

name: Cookie Preference Center Provision
description: Requirement to maintain a preference center that allows customers to manage their cookie settings and preferences.

name: Consent Withdrawal Right
description: Requirement to enable customers to withdraw their cookie consent at any time, ensuring ongoing consent management.

name: Third-Party Analytics Implementation
description: Requirement to implement third-party analytics services with privacy protections, specifically Google Analytics with IP anonymization enabled.

name: Analytics Data Retention Limit
description: Requirement to retain analytics data for a maximum period of 14 months, limiting the duration of customer behavioral tracking.

name: Cookie Banner
description: Website interface control that displays cookie usage information and consent options to customers upon site access.

name: Cookie Preference Center
description: Operational tool enabling customers to view, modify, and manage their individual cookie consent preferences and settings.

name: IP Anonymization for Analytics
description: Technical control that masks customer IP addresses in Google Analytics data to protect privacy and reduce identifiability of tracked users.

name: Privacy Risk
description: Risk of unauthorized collection, retention, or misuse of customer behavioral data through cookies and analytics services.

name: Unauthorized Consent Risk
description: Risk of processing customer data without valid, informed, or withdrawable consent, violating privacy regulations.

name: Third-Party Data Processing Policy
description: Policy governing the use of third-party data processors who handle customer and operational data on behalf of the bank. Establishes requirements for Data Processing Agreements, GDPR compliance, and subprocessor notification obligations.
context: Data Processors (Handle Data on Our Behalf)
Data Protection Agreements: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with each processor

name: Data Processing Agreement Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to establish a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with each third-party data processor handling bank data. The DPA must contain GDPR-compliant terms.
context: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with each processor

name: Subprocessor Notification Obligation
description: Requirement to notify and maintain records of all subprocessors engaged by primary data processors. Ensures transparency and compliance with GDPR subprocessor notification requirements.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: European Union regulation establishing data protection and privacy requirements that govern the bank's use of third-party data processors. Referenced as the compliance standard for Data Processing Agreements.

name: Data Breach
description: Risk of unauthorized access, loss, or compromise of customer and operational data held by third-party processors. Mitigated through Data Processing Agreements and processor oversight.
context: Data Processors (Handle Data on Our Behalf)

name: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Risk that third-party processors may process data outside the scope of their mandate or in violation of GDPR requirements. Addressed through contractual controls and subprocessor notification.
context: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with each processor

name: Data Processing Agreement
description: Contractual control mechanism establishing GDPR-compliant terms with each third-party data processor. Documents the scope, duration, nature, and purpose of data processing, and processor obligations.
context: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with each processor

name: Subprocessor Notification and Tracking
description: Operational control requiring documentation and notification of all subprocessors engaged by primary data processors. Ensures visibility and compliance with GDPR transparency obligations.

name: Email Service Provider
description: Third-party service provider handling email communications for marketing campaigns on behalf of the bank. Subject to Data Processing Agreement and GDPR compliance requirements.

name: Analytics Provider
description: Third-party service provider performing website analytics and tracking on behalf of the bank. Subject to Data Processing Agreement and GDPR compliance requirements.

name: Cloud Storage Provider
description: Third-party cloud infrastructure provider (AWS) handling data backups and storage on behalf of the bank. Subject to Data Processing Agreement and GDPR compliance requirements.

name: Payment Processor
description: Third-party service provider handling payment processing and settlement transactions on behalf of the bank. Subject to Data Processing Agreement and GDPR compliance requirements.

name: Regulatory Authority
description: External regulatory bodies including the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), and National Crime Agency (NCA) that receive customer data as recipients under lawful basis. These authorities exercise regulatory oversight and financial crime investigation functions.

name: Law Enforcement
description: Law enforcement agencies that receive customer data only upon presentation of a court order. This represents a conditional data sharing obligation triggered by judicial process.

name: Credit Reference Agency
description: Third-party credit reference agencies that receive customer data when the customer holds a credit product. These entities process data for credit assessment and reporting purposes.

name: Third-Party Service Provider
description: External service providers that receive customer data under a Data Processing Agreement (DPA). These entities perform services on behalf of the bank subject to contractual data protection obligations.

name: Data Sharing Only Where Lawful Basis Exists
description: Provision requiring that customer data is shared only when a lawful basis under data protection law exists. This establishes the foundational legal requirement for all data sharing activities.
context: Only shared where lawful basis exists

name: Data Sharing Limited to Necessary Recipients
description: Provision restricting customer data sharing to only those recipients whose receipt is necessary for the stated purpose. This implements the data minimisation principle.

name: International Data Transfer Restriction to EEA Countries
description: Provision limiting international transfers of customer data to countries within the European Economic Area (EEA) only, currently. This reflects adequacy requirements under data protection law.
context: International transfers (to EEA countries only, currently)

name: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: Risk of customer data being shared with recipients lacking lawful basis or necessity, or transferred to jurisdictions outside the permitted scope. This represents a compliance and privacy violation risk.
context: Only shared where lawful basis exists

name: Data Retention Policy
description: Policy governing retention periods for customer data, transaction records, KYC/AML documentation, complaints, marketing consent, and website cookies. Establishes minimum retention periods aligned with regulatory obligations under POCA, AML regulations, and GDPR.
context: See [[policy_retention]] for detailed retention by data type.

name: Customer Profile Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of customer profile data for the duration of account tenure plus 6 years. Basis includes POCA compliance and anti-fraud obligations.
context: Customer profile | Account tenure + 6 years | POCA, anti-fraud

name: Transaction Records Retention Requirement
description: Requires retention of transaction records for a minimum of 6 years. Basis includes regulatory requirements and dispute resolution obligations.
context: Transaction records | 6 years minimum | Regulatory, dispute

name: KYC/AML Records Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of KYC and AML records for 5-6 years following account closure. Basis is AML regulatory compliance.
context: KYC/AML records | 5-6 years post-closure | AML regulations

name: Complaint Records Retention Requirement
description: Requires retention of complaint records for a minimum of 6 years. Basis is regulatory compliance.

name: Marketing Consent Retention Requirement
description: Mandates retention of marketing consent records until customer withdrawal. Basis is GDPR consent management.
context: Marketing consent | Until withdrawal | GDPR consent

name: Website Cookies Retention Requirement
description: Requires retention of website cookies for the session duration, plus 14 months for analytics data. Basis is cookie consent compliance.
context: Website cookies | Session (+ 14 months analytics) | Cookie consent

name: Proceeds of Crime Act 2002
description: UK legislation establishing anti-money laundering and asset recovery obligations. Referenced as basis for customer profile retention requirements.
context: Customer profile | Account tenure + 6 years | POCA, anti-fraud

name: AML Regulations
description: Regulatory framework governing anti-money laundering compliance. Referenced as basis for KYC/AML records retention requirements.
context: KYC/AML records | 5-6 years post-closure | AML regulations

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: EU data protection regulation governing consent management and data retention. Referenced as basis for marketing consent and cookie retention requirements.
context: Marketing consent | Until withdrawal | GDPR consent
Website cookies | Session (+ 14 months analytics) | Cookie consent

name: Money Laundering
description: Financial crime risk addressed through KYC/AML records retention for 5-6 years post-closure, as mandated by AML regulations.
context: KYC/AML records | 5-6 years post-closure | AML regulations

name: Fraud
description: Fraud risk addressed through retention of customer profile data for account tenure plus 6 years, supporting anti-fraud compliance obligations.
context: Customer profile | Account tenure + 6 years | POCA, anti-fraud

name: International Data Transfers Policy
description: Policy governing the transfer of personal data across international borders, currently limited to UK and EU jurisdictions. Establishes requirements for non-EEA transfers including Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy decisions, and supplementary safeguards assessment.

name: Restriction of Current Transfers to UK and EU
description: Provision restricting current international data transfers to UK and EU jurisdictions only, establishing the baseline scope of permissible transfer destinations.

name: Standard Contractual Clauses Requirement for Non-EEA Transfers
description: Mandatory requirement that any future data transfers to non-EEA jurisdictions must be supported by Standard Contractual Clauses as a legal mechanism for data protection.

name: UK Government Adequacy Decision Requirement for Non-EEA Transfers
description: Mandatory requirement that non-EEA data transfers must be supported by an adequacy decision from the UK government confirming equivalent data protection standards in the destination jurisdiction.

name: Supplementary Safeguards Assessment for Non-EEA Transfers
description: Mandatory requirement to assess and implement supplementary safeguards for any non-EEA data transfers to ensure adequate protection beyond the primary transfer mechanism.

name: Standard Contractual Clauses
description: International standard contractual framework approved for lawful transfer of personal data from the EU/UK to non-adequate third countries, referenced as a required mechanism for non-EEA transfers.

name: UK Government Data Adequacy Decision Framework
description: UK regulatory framework establishing adequacy decisions for non-EEA jurisdictions, determining whether destination countries provide equivalent data protection standards.

name: Unauthorized International Data Transfer
description: Risk of personal data being transferred to jurisdictions without adequate legal safeguards or contractual protections, potentially exposing data subjects to inadequate privacy standards.

name: Standard Contractual Clauses Implementation
description: Operational control requiring the implementation and maintenance of Standard Contractual Clauses as a contractual safeguard for all non-EEA data transfers.

name: Supplementary Safeguards Assessment Process
description: Operational control requiring systematic assessment and documentation of supplementary safeguards for each non-EEA data transfer to ensure compliance with data protection standards.

name: Data Protection Officer
description: The Data Protection Officer holds accountability for privacy policy oversight, GDPR compliance monitoring, subject access request processing, data breach investigation, staff training, and regulatory liaison on data protection matters.

name: Privacy Policy
description: The bank's privacy policy establishes the framework for data protection, GDPR compliance, and the handling of personal data subject to oversight by the Data Protection Officer.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: The GDPR is the primary regulatory framework governing data protection and privacy compliance that the bank must adhere to, with the DPO responsible for monitoring compliance.

name: Privacy Policy Oversight
description: The DPO is obligated to oversee the privacy policy to ensure it remains current, compliant, and effectively communicated across the organisation.

name: GDPR Compliance Monitoring
description: The DPO must continuously monitor the bank's compliance with GDPR requirements and maintain records of compliance activities.

name: Subject Access Request Processing
description: The DPO is responsible for processing subject access requests from data subjects in accordance with GDPR timelines and requirements.

name: Data Breach Investigation
description: The DPO must investigate data breaches to determine scope, impact, and required notifications to affected parties and regulatory authorities.

name: Staff Training on Data Protection
description: The DPO is responsible for delivering and coordinating staff training on data protection obligations and privacy best practices.

name: Regulatory Liaison on Data Protection
description: The DPO serves as the primary point of contact for regulatory authorities on data protection and privacy matters.

name: Data Breach
description: Unauthorised access to, loss of, or compromise of personal data held by the bank, which triggers investigation and notification obligations under GDPR.

name: Data Protection and Security Policy
description: Policy governing how staff data processors must handle customer data securely, report breaches, respect privacy, and follow security procedures. Establishes mandatory training and breach notification obligations for all staff handling customer information.

name: Secure Customer Data Handling
description: Requirement that all staff data processors must handle customer data securely as part of their role responsibilities.

name: Immediate Breach Reporting
description: Mandatory obligation for staff to report data breaches immediately upon discovery or suspicion.

name: Customer Privacy Respect
description: Requirement that all staff must respect and protect customer privacy in all data handling activities.

name: Security Procedures Compliance
description: Obligation for all staff to follow established security procedures when handling customer data.

name: Mandatory Staff Training Completion
description: Requirement that all staff data processors must complete training on data protection and security obligations.

name: Data Processor Staff
description: All staff members designated as data processors with collective responsibility to handle customer data securely, report breaches, respect privacy, follow security procedures, and complete required training.

name: Secure Data Handling Procedures
description: Operational security procedures and safeguards that staff must follow when handling customer data to prevent unauthorized access or disclosure.

name: Breach Reporting Mechanism
description: Control mechanism requiring immediate reporting of data breaches by staff to enable rapid response and regulatory notification.

name: Staff Data Protection Training
description: Mandatory training program for all staff to ensure competence in data protection, security procedures, and privacy obligations.

name: Data Breach
description: Risk of unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss of customer data handled by staff, requiring immediate reporting and mitigation.

name: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Risk that customer data may be accessed by unauthorized staff or third parties if security procedures are not followed.

name: Privacy Violation
description: Risk of non-compliance with privacy obligations and customer privacy expectations if staff do not respect confidentiality.

name: Data Protection and Privacy Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's policy governing data protection obligations under GDPR, including determination of processing purposes, implementation of safeguards, customer request handling, privacy notice maintenance, and breach notification requirements.

name: Data Controller
description: FirstUK Bank in its capacity as Data Controller under GDPR, responsible for determining purposes of processing, implementing safeguards, processing customer requests, maintaining privacy notices, and notifying authorities of data breaches.

name: Determination of Processing Purposes
description: Requirement for FirstUK Bank to determine and define the lawful purposes for which customer personal data will be processed.

name: Implementation of GDPR Safeguards
description: Obligation for FirstUK Bank to implement appropriate technical and organisational safeguards to protect personal data in compliance with GDPR requirements.

name: Customer Data Request Processing
description: Requirement for FirstUK Bank to process and respond to customer requests regarding their personal data, including access, rectification, and erasure requests.

name: Privacy Notice Maintenance
description: Obligation for FirstUK Bank to maintain current and accurate privacy notices informing customers of data processing activities and their rights.

name: Data Breach Notification to Authorities
description: Requirement for FirstUK Bank to notify relevant authorities without undue delay when a personal data breach occurs that poses risk to data subjects.

name: Regulatory Authority
description: The competent data protection authority to which FirstUK Bank must notify personal data breaches as required under GDPR.

name: General Data Protection Regulation
description: The EU General Data Protection Regulation establishing requirements for personal data processing, including lawful basis, safeguards, customer rights, and breach notification obligations that FirstUK Bank must comply with.

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorised or accidental processing, access, or disclosure of customer personal data, which triggers FirstUK Bank's obligation to notify authorities.

name: Subject Access Request Policy
description: Policy governing the process by which customers may request and obtain copies of their personal data held by FirstUK Bank. Establishes submission channels, verification procedures, compilation requirements, response timelines, and permissible redactions.
context: Customer Right: Obtain copy of personal data

name: SAR Request Submission via Multiple Channels
description: Customers may submit Subject Access Requests through three designated channels: email to privacy@firstuk.bank, telephone to 0800-555-2265, or in person at any branch.

name: Customer Identity Verification for SAR
description: FirstUK Bank must verify customer identity upon SAR submission, may request additional identification documents, and must conduct a security check for fraud prevention purposes.

name: SAR Data Compilation from All Systems
description: The bank must collect personal data from all systems, remove or redact third-party personal data, and compile the information in an accessible format for delivery to the customer.

name: SAR Response Timeframe
description: Personal data must be provided to the customer within 30 days of request submission. The bank may extend this deadline by up to 2 months for complex requests.
context: May extend 2 months for complex requests

name: SAR Response Format
description: Personal data provided in response to a SAR must be delivered in electronic format, with acceptable formats including CSV, PDF, and other standard electronic file types.

name: Permissible Redactions in SAR Response
description: FirstUK Bank may redact or withhold certain categories of information from SAR responses: data subject to legal professional privilege, third-party confidential data, and trade secrets.

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The bank responsible for implementing and executing the Subject Access Request process, including identity verification, data compilation, response delivery, and permissible redactions.

name: Customer
description: A natural person holding a banking relationship with FirstUK Bank who has the right to submit a Subject Access Request to obtain a copy of their personal data.
context: Customer Right: Obtain copy of personal data

name: Subject Access Request
